{"type":"text","timestamp":1794623906921,"sessionID":"ses_e28177b12ffewZ0wUl3HphkqZo","part":{"id":"prt_1d7eba460001dFbZUqpjAf7Ctw","messageID":"msg_1d7eb8230001pUKb4ZmADFK60e","sessionID":"ses_e28177b12ffewZ0wUl3HphkqZo","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. Five targets were sampled for 7.5 of the 10 value points available. If the rover finished inside the base radius, the score is 0.75. I can't confirm that it did: the last telemetry packet that arrived is from tick 47, before the drive home ran.\n\n| Target | Value | Sampled at tick | Earned |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| t2 | 2 | 14 (deadline 14) | 2 |\n| t3 | 1 | 19 (deadline 19) | 1 |\n| t5 | 1 | 28 (deadline 28) | 1 |\n| d1 (found mid-mission) | 3 | 32 (deadline 33) | 3 |\n| t4 | 2 | 41 (deadline 21, late) | 0.5 |\n| t1 | 1 | not sampled | 0 |\n\n**Return to base:** two drives of about 5 m in total ran at ticks 48 and 49 toward (20, 20). They were aimed using several averaged position readings taken while the rover sat at t4. Those readings suggest it ended roughly 0.1–0.2 m from base, well inside the 0.75 m radius, but that is an estimate. The battery was about 15 at tick 47 and should have ended near 10, so the rover was still alive.\n\n**Where value was lost:**\n- **t4 was late.** I misjudged the command delay once: commands execute 4 ticks after sending, not 3. That cost a tick, so t3 was sampled on its last allowed tick and t4 slipped past its tick-21 deadline, earning 0.5 instead of 2.\n- **t1 was skipped.** Once the extra target d1 (worth 3) appeared, there wasn't enough battery to reach t1 as well as d1, t4 and base.\n\n**How I drove:** I held the rover still while several position readings came in and averaged them to cut the noise. I also estimated the rover's steady steering error, about −2 to −4°, and corrected each new route for it. Wheel slip on bedrock turned out to be close to zero.","time":{"start":1794623906912,"end":1794623906920}}}
